messages.subject: bug in trans_coordinate
parts:
Here's a bug that I encountered in ggplot2. I works with
"scale_y_log10()" instead of coord_trans(), but I want to get the
coordinate system drawn like this (but on the y-axis):

[1] http://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/83/LogLogPlot_of_Line.GIF


Sebastian

ggplot() +
layer(data=df, mapping=aes(x=factor(name),y=total,fill=factor(name)),
geom="bar") +

mapping=aes(x=factor(name),y=total,ymin=total.l,ymax=total.h), size=1,

The code you gave didn't run as written, and had some other problems
as well. But I was able to get to what I think your problem is. I'm
going to set aside that you seem like you are trying to make a
"dynamite plot" (http://biostat.mc.vanderbilt.edu/twiki/pub/Main/
TatsukiRcode/Poster3.pdf) and focus on the error.

A minimized example:

DF <- structure(list(name = structure(c(2L, 1L), .Label = c("C", "D"
), class = "factor"), total = c(1, 2.02961986153729)), .Names =
c("name",
"total"), row.names = c(NA, -2L), class = "data.frame")

ggplot() +
layer(data=DF, mapping=aes(x=name,y=total), geom="bar",
stat="identity") +
coord_trans(y = "log10")
# Error in if (length(from) == 1 || length(to) == 1 || from[1] ==
from[2] || :
# missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

ggplot() +
layer(data=DF, mapping=aes(x=name,y=total), geom="bar",
stat="identity") +
scale_y_log10()
# produces a plot without error or warning

I am also surprised that these behave differently, but I would expect
both to not work. If you look at the un-transformed version:

ggplot() +
layer(data=DF, mapping=aes(x=name,y=total), geom="bar",
stat="identity")

you have a regular bar plot with the y-axis ranging from 0 to 2. If I
log10 transform these two points, I get -Inf, 0.3. Bar plots start at
0, and 0 on a log scale is minus infinity; bar plots and log scale
axes are inherently incompatible. (Granted, deducing that from the
error message given would take working through details of the source
code.) I would recommend looking at the pointrange geom.

DF <- structure(list(name = structure(c(4L, 3L, 3L, 1L, 2L), .Label =
c("xxx",
"xxx xxxxxx", "xxx xxxxxx (xx xxxxxxx)", "xxxxxx"), class =
"factor"),
total = c(1, 2.02961986153729, 9.46638602185986,
12.8070144295387,
111.006948494915), mad = c(0, 0.7413, 551.5272, 653.8266,
5537.511), mean = c(79.0240480961924, 162.670731707317, 746.576,
1010.038, 8754.674), median = c(0, 0.5, 383, 441, 7595.5),
total.h = c(1.00041195196771, 2.0302456440019, 9.46857659298375,
12.8099557850261, 111.020044365812), total.l =
c(0.999588048032286,
2.02899407907269, 9.46419545073598, 12.8040730740514,
110.993852624018
), type = c(2L, 2L, 2L, 1L, 1L)), .Names = c("name", "total",
"mad", "mean", "median", "total.h", "total.l", "type"), class =
"data.frame", row.names = c("1",
"2", "3", "4", "5"))

ggplot() +
layer(data=DF,
mapping=aes(x=factor(name),y=total,ymin=total.l,ymax=total.h),geom="pointrange")

ggplot() +
layer(data=DF,
mapping=aes(x=factor(name),y=total,ymin=total.l,ymax=total.h),
geom="pointrange") +
scale_y_log10()
